blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Scenario S4, a helper that explores a legacy system and generates boilerplate. A check reports `unknown-server: wiki (explorer)`. What does the finding mean?

options.text: A header holds a credential that somebody typed in by hand, in plain text
options.says: Ruled out because that is another finding: "`literal-secret`: a header or environment entry whose name says token, key, secret or authorization".

options.text: A reference points at an entry that the project file never defines
options.says: The finding is about a name that is not configured.

options.text: A subagent has no tools line and inherits everything
options.says: Ruled out for the same reason: "`agent-inherits-all` and `agent-bare-bash`: a subagent with no `tools` line, or with the shell tool in it".

options.text: A permission rule approves the whole tool rather than one path of it
options.says: Ruled out because that is a third: "`bare-write-allowed`: an allow rule that approves the whole `Edit` or `Write` tool."

questions.stem: Scenario S4, a helper that explores a legacy system and generates boilerplate. Which entry does the check for typed-in credentials report?

options.text: A header named Authorization whose value is `Bearer <token>`
options.says: The check reports a secret-looking name whose value has no reference: "a header or environment entry whose name says token, key, secret or authorization and whose value has no `${` reference".

options.text: A header named Authorization whose value is `Bearer ${TICKETS_TOKEN}`
options.says: Ruled out because its value is a reference: "whose value has no `${` reference".

options.text: A header named X-Trace whose value is `abc`, sent with every request
options.says: Ruled out because the name says nothing of a secret: "whose name says token, key, secret or authorization".

options.text: A variable named REGION whose value is `eu`, passed to the local server
options.says: Ruled out for the same reason: "whose name says token, key, secret or authorization".

questions.stem: Scenario S4, a helper that explores a legacy system and generates boilerplate. Which explorer definition passes the practice's explorer case?

options.text: A description that starts `Use when`, and a tools line of `Read`, `Grep` and `Glob`
options.says: The page states the case: "The explorer case passes when its description starts with `Use when`, its `tools` line exists, and the line lists only `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob` and `mcp__docs__search`."

options.text: A description that says `Explores the legacy system`, and the same tools line
options.says: Ruled out by the first condition: "its description starts with `Use when`".

options.text: A description that starts `Use when`, and a tools line of `Read`, `Grep` and `Bash`
options.says: Ruled out by the last: "the line lists only `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob` and `mcp__docs__search`".

options.text: A description that starts `Use when`, and no tools line at all
options.says: Ruled out by the second: "its `tools` line exists".

questions.stem: Scenario S4, a helper that explores a legacy system and generates boilerplate. A team writes the header as `Bearer ${TICKETS_TOKEN:-dev-token}` so the tools work on a fresh clone. What is wrong with it?

options.text: A default is applied to the address and never to a header
options.says: Ruled out because a header is one of the places where it works: "`${VAR:-default}` expands to the variable if it is set and to the default otherwise".

options.text: Expansion in headers handles only the plain form of a reference
options.says: Ruled out because expansion has both forms: "Expansion of `${VAR}` and `${VAR:-default}` works in a server's `command`, `args`, `env`, `url` and `headers`".

options.text: The default puts a usable credential into a committed file
options.says: A default for a token is a credential in the file.

options.text: A file that carries a default cannot be shared through version control
options.says: Ruled out because sharing is the file's purpose: "The `.mcp.json` of a project is committed so that the team shares its servers."
